subject: math-aa-sl
title: A graphical solution without a closed form

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the solution to three significant figures, stating the graphs you use.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why there is only one positive solution.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: For a new parameter $k>0$, the equation is $e^{-x}=x/k$. Find k so that x=1 is the solution. Then explain whether doubling this k makes the positive solution larger or smaller.

steps.text: Graph $y=e^{-x}$ and $y=x/1$ and find their intersection.
For x>0, the exponential decreases strictly and the straight line increases strictly.
At x=0 the exponential is larger; for sufficiently large x the line is larger, so exactly one intersection occurs.
Doubling k halves the slope of y=x/k; at the original intersection the line is now below the exponential.

subject: math-aa-sl
title: Height from a quadratic model
stem: A model for a ball height is $h(t)=12t-2t^2$ metres, where t is seconds and $0\leq t\leq 6$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the greatest height and the time at which it occurs using completed-square form.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the time interval during which the ball is above half its maximum height.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of height during the first second and during the final second of the stated flight. Explain the relationship.

steps.text: The maximum is $18$ m at $t=3$ s.
Both boundary times lie in the physical domain; the strict inequality excludes the boundary times.
Use $[h(b)-h(a)]/(b-a)$ on [0,1] and on the final one-second interval.
The rates are $10$ m s⁻¹ and $-10$ m s⁻¹ respectively.
The quadratic height model is symmetric about its maximum, giving equal magnitudes with opposite signs.

verification.method: Independent symbolic/numeric and mathematical reasoning checks
verification.notes: Displayed parameters were recalculated; see the per-record AA SL author-review ledger. Vertex checked algebraically; half-height roots substituted and confirmed inside stated flight domain.
